title: Saddle/valley detector for per-tooth patch separation
description:
Context: PATCH-11 (Yoshizawa crest-line detection) + the PATCH-11-diagnostic fixes (crest-preserving merge pass, adaptive p95 principal-magnitude threshold) land the cranium, zygomatic, orbital and nasal regions as clean patches on the skull. Individual teeth remain fused into one mandible blob.

Root cause is algorithmic, not tunable. `CrestLineDetector` traces ridges/valleys via NMS along the principal eigenvector, walking in the direction of *least* bending. Between two adjacent teeth, the valley runs ALONG the gum line, not ACROSS the inter-tooth gap — so the detector geometrically cannot emit the perpendicular cuts needed to separate teeth. Parameter tuning cannot fix this; a different detector is required.

Proposed approach: add a saddle-point / umbilic detector on top of the existing `PrincipalDirectionField`. For each vertex:
 (a) SADDLE: sign change in `κ₁·κ₂` across the 1-ring → emit a short cut perpendicular to the dominant principal direction (walk 3–5 edges along the direction that separates, both ± sides).
 (b) UMBILIC at high curvature: `|κ₁ − κ₂|` below a threshold AND curvature magnitude above p95 → tooth-tip candidate; emit a radial cut into surrounding convex material.

Union the resulting "separator edges" with the existing crest/principal/dihedral feature-edge set at SemanticPatchDecomposer.java line 236, so region growing terminates at them.

Critical files:
- ixdar-app/src/main/java/ixdar/geometry/mesh/data/CrestLineDetector.java — the Yoshizawa detector (reference implementation style)
- ixdar-app/src/main/java/ixdar/geometry/mesh/data/PrincipalDirectionField.java — provides κMax, κMin, dirMax, dirMin (do not recompute)
- ixdar-app/src/main/java/ixdar/geometry/mesh/data/SemanticPatchDecomposer.java — integration point at the allFeatureEdges union
- ixdar-app/src/main/java/ixdar/geometry/mesh/data/PatchRenderer.java — diagnostic `renderFeatureEdgeMultiview(mode=PATCHES_VS_CREST)` will show if new cuts become honored patch boundaries

Test mesh: /Users/acw28/Code/KriegEterna/web/static/ixdar/obj/voyage_skull_ref.obj.

Do NOT weaken the existing threshold changes. Verify the skull's cranium, zygomatic, orbital and nasal regions remain cleanly patched after adding the new detector — it should be additive, not replace existing logic.
definition-of-done:
1. New class `SaddleValleyDetector` (or equivalent) consuming `PrincipalDirectionField` + mesh topology, producing a `Set<Long>` of "separator edges".
2. Integrated into `SemanticPatchDecomposer.decomposeWithDiagnostics` so diagnostic rendering can show the new cuts.
3. On voyage_skull_ref.obj with resolution=128, each individual tooth appears as its own patch in `PatchRenderer.renderMultiviewFlat` — inspect the Right view (the face-on render, per the 2024-era view naming) and count distinct patches across the tooth row. Target: ≥12 per-tooth patches for the upper row.
4. Cranium / zygomatic / orbital / nasal regions are NOT regressed — same or better feature alignment vs. the pre-change state.
5. `PatchRenderer.renderFeatureEdgeMultiview` in PATCHES_VS_CREST mode shows green (honored) edges between teeth.
testing-plan:
1. Run the headless verifier `/tmp/VerifyFeatureEdges.java` (template from the PATCH-11-diagnostic session) against voyage_skull_ref.obj. Confirm the teeth region now shows individual patches in flat render + honored-green crest edges between them.
2. Run `PatchDecomposerCLI decompose` on the same mesh and sanity-check patch count is not runaway (expect ~200–400 patches total after the new detector; anything over 1000 means the new detector is firing too broadly).
3. Spot-check cranium/zygomatic/orbital/nasal regions — compare flat multiview before/after to confirm no regression in already-working areas.
4. Render `PatchRenderer.renderFeatureEdgeMultiview(STAGES mode)` to visualize where the new detector fires vs the existing dihedral/principal/crest sets.
